title: Fabrication of Nanomechanical Biosensors to Map 3D Surface Strain in Live Cells and Tissue
protocol: Design a square-lattice mesh using AutoCAD software.
Arrange pattern designs and variations to fill a transparency photomask.
Clean square glass wafers with ethanol.
Flame dry the cleaned glass wafers.
Spin-coat the glass with Photoresist SPR-220.3 at 5000 rpm for 20 seconds.
Bake the wafers on an 115°C hot plate for 90 seconds.
Place the photomask with the patterned side down on top of the photoresist coated wafer and expose to ultraviolet (UV) light through the transparency photomask.
Bake the patterned wafer on a 115°C hot plate for 90 sec following UV exposure.
Develop the cured wafer for 1 min using MF-26A developer and wash twice in ddH2O.
Prepare Sylgard 184 (Dow Corning) polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer per the manufacturer’s directions by mixing 10 parts base to 1 part curing agent (by weight).
Mix Sylgard for 2 min at 2000 rpm using a Thinky-Conditioning mixer, followed by defoaming at 2000 rpm.
Cast PDMS over the patterned photoresist-coated glass wafer inside a 150 mm petri dish and place in a 65°C oven for at least 4 hours to cure the PDMS.
Cover the glass wafer completely with PDMS, aiming for a thickness of approximately 5 mm.
Place PDMS into a vacuum chamber and remove air bubbles by curing at 65°C for 30 minutes.
Cut square PDMS stamps measuring approximately 1 cm² using a new razor blade from the ~5 mm thick PDMS layer.
Avoid damaging the patterned region when cutting the stamp.
Ensure there are no unpatterned areas around the edges of the stamp face to prevent air trapping during patterning.
Cut a notch out of the corner on the back side of each stamp for identification purposes.
Add a 10 µL aliquot of the Alexa-555 dye to 500 µL of fibronectin (1 mg/mL) in 250 µL of SE buffer and allow to incubate at room temperature in the dark for 1 hour.

Transfer the solution to a dialysis cassette and place into SE buffer for 2 hours, followed by phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) for 2 hours, and finally DI water overnight, all at 4°C in a dark environment.
Clean and sonicate round glass coverslips (25 mm) in a 100% ethanol solution for 1 hour.
Prepare a 2% g/mL poly(N-isopropyl acrylamide) (PIPAAm) by solubilizing in 1-Butanol overnight with frequent vortexing.
Spin-coat cleaned coverslips at 6000 rpm for 1 min and 37 sec with 200 µL of the PIPAAm solution.
Place spin-coated coverslips into a 150 mm culture dish under UV light for 15 minutes to sterilize.
Wash patterned PDMS stamps in 50% EtOH for 30 min in sonicator bath.
Remove stamps from ethanol solution and dry inside of a biosafety cabinet with nitrogen air.
Prepare a 50 µg/mL fibronectin solution in sterile ddH2O.
Prepare a 50 ug/mL Alexa-555 fibronctin solution in sterile ddH2O.
Make a working solution of 40/60% labeled to unlabeled 50 µg/mL fibronectin in DI water.
Pipette approximately 150 µL of the 40/60 working solution onto each stamp making sure that the entire surface of the stamp is covered.
Cover the culture dish with foil.
Incubate the labeled fibronectin solution for 1 hour in the biosafety cabinet.
Wash stamps by dipping them into a 10 cm culture dish filled with ddH2O twice in two separate dishes.
Dry stamps with nitrogen gas on all sides.
Gently place the stamp patterned side down onto the PIPAAm coverslips using forceps, avoiding air bubbles.
Press lightly on the corners of the stamp with forceps to adhere it to the PIPAAm coverslip.
Allow the stamp and PIPAAm coverslip to sit in the biosafety cabinet for 1 hour covered in foil.
Gently remove the stamp from the PIPAAm using forceps.
Hold down the glass coverslip with a second pair of forceps as you peel off the PDMS stamp.
Pry the stamp off towards one edge and lift once it is completely detached from the coverslip.
Check the integrity of the patterned fibronectin on the PIPAAm coverslip before transferring to a biological tissue.
Use a microscope with compatible excitation and emission filters depending on the fluorescent protein conjugated to the ECM protein.
The easiest way to check the pattern is by stereo fluorescence or inverted EPI-fluorescence.
Use an inverted fluorescence microscope and a 10X or 20X air objective to image the patterned fibronectin on culture dishes.
Find the focal plane of the thin patterned fibronectin.
Outline the area on the coverslip that will be transferred to the gelatin carrier with a marker.
Make a 20% w/v solution of Gelatin type A by dissolving in ddH2O at 40°C or appropriate aqueous solution.
Adjust the aqueous buffer for the carrier according to cell or tissue specificity for better cell survival during transfer.
Use a 10 mm punch to create circular molds from a 1.5 mm thick silicone sheet.
Keep the gelatin solution warm at 40°C to prevent it from gelling.
Place a silicone mold onto an ethanol-cleaned glass slide.
Place the glass slide on top of a 40°C hot plate.
Pipette warmed gelatin into the silicone mold.
Remove the glass slide from the hot plate and allow to cool at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Transfer the glass slide to a 150 mm culture dish.
Allow the gelatin to set further at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Place fibronectin-patterned PIPAAm-coated glass coverslips with patterned side facing down onto the gelatin carriers inside of a biosafety cabinet for 1 minute.

Slowly add sterile room temperature ddH₂O between the glass coverslips and the gelatin carrier to cause dissolution of the PIPAAm and subsequent release and transfer of the NMBS to the top surface of the gelatin.
Tap lightly on the coverslip if an air bubble is trapped to free the bubble.
Add more ddH₂O to flush out any trapped air bubbles.
Use a small gauge needle gently to vacuum out the air bubble.
Remove all remaining water surrounding the NMBS-gelatin carrier after transfer.
Ensure the gelatin carrier is stored in a sealed container at 4°C until ready for tissue application.
Remove media from cells or tissue before applying the NMBS.
Lift the NMBS-gelatin carrier from the glass slide using forceps.
Keep the gelatin carrier at 4°C to improve handleability.
Place the gelatin carrier NMBS face down onto the tissue or cells.
Avoid moving the carrier around once applied to the tissue.
Apply light pressure if needed to assist in initial adhesion of the NMBS.
Place the tissue with the gelatin and NMBS applied back into a 37°C incubator for 3-5 minutes.
Add warmed media to help rehydrate the tissue and prevent cell death after the gelatin begins to melt.
Return the tissue to the incubator for 5-7 minutes.
Proceed with subsequent media changes and fluorescence imaging experiments.
